'''Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin''' ({{IPA|ga|ˈiːvʲən̠ʲ n̠ʲiː ˈhuːl̠ʲəwaːnʲ|pron}}; born 25 October 1983) is an Irish academic, teacher, broadcaster and high-profile science communicator.<ref name="Sunday Times profile ANiS"/> She also won the [[Rose of Tralee (festival)|Rose of Tralee]] contest in 2005 and toured internationally as the lead singer of an Irish traditional music band. In 2022, she was appointed to chair a national forum on biodiversity loss, presenting its report to [[Taoiseach]] [[Leo Varadkar]] in April 2023, and presenting on the topic to a committee of the UN General Assembly later that month.

==Early life and education==
Ní Shúilleabháin is a native of the village of [[Carnacon]] near [[Ballyglass]], [[County Mayo]].<ref name="WP050816">{{cite news |url=http://www.westernpeople.ie/news/story/?trs=cwgbgbojmh |title=Aoibhinn is all set to blossom in Tralee |last=Esler |first=Cróna |date=16 August 2005 |newspaper=[[Western People]] |accessdate=22 February 2010 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110814060244/http://www.westernpeople.ie/news/story/?trs=cwgbgbojmh |archivedate=14 August 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="II050824">{{cite news |url=http://www.independent.ie/national-news/bookies-favourite-aoibhinn-is-the-new-rose-246488.html |title=Bookies' favourite Aoibhinn is the new Rose |last=Anderson |first=Nicola |date=24 August 2005 |newspaper=[[Irish Independent]] |accessdate=22 February 2010 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026095508/http://www.independent.ie/national-news/bookies-favourite-aoibhinn-is-the-new-rose-246488.html |archivedate=26 October 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref> Her parents were teachers,<ref name="ThisMuchIKnow"/> her father, Art, from County Galway, being the principal of Carnacon National School, and her mother, Maire, vice-principal of a Gaelscoil in Castlebar.<ref name="KeenToMapANewWayForward"/><ref name="Sunday Times profile ANiS"/> She was the eldest of a family of six, with five brothers.<ref name="ThisMuchIKnow"/> She has credited her success and interest in some aspects of maths and science to a good teacher of maths in primary school, and to a secondary school science teacher, Mr McMonagle.<ref name="KeenToMapANewWayForward"/><ref name="Green_n_Red_ivw"/> She grew up speaking both English and Irish, and remained a Gaeilgeoir, still thinking partly in Irish as an adult.<ref name="Green_n_Red_ivw"/>

She entered [[University College Dublin]] (UCD) with an Entrance Scholarship for high marks in the [[Leaving Certificate (Ireland)|Leaving Certificate]].  She received further scholarships from [[Bord na Gaeilge]], which included residence for her first two years at UCD in an Irish-speaking hall on campus, and a requirement to organise Irish-language campus events.<ref name="Green_n_Red_ivw">{{Cite web |last=Green and Red |date=2005 |title=A Rose by Any Other Name . . . |url=http://castlebar.ie/photos/greenandred/aoibhinn/aoibhinn.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070311072938/http://castlebar.ie/photos/greenandred/aoibhinn/aoibhinn.htm |archive-date=11 March 2007 |access-date=23 April 2023 |website=Castlebar.ie (local news site)}}</ref><ref name="siliconrepublic"/> During her studies, she spent the summer of 2004 working at [[CERN]] in Geneva.<ref name="siliconrepublic"/> She graduated with a first-class honours degree in Theoretical Physics in 2005.<ref name="siliconrepublic"/>

==Academic career and science communication==
Ní Shúilleabháin obtained funding for a four-year masters and doctorate in Biological Mathematics<ref name="Indo faces">{{cite news |title=Focus on faces: Aoibhinn Ni Shuilleabhain |work=Irish Independent |date=21 August 2006}}</ref> at [[University College London]] but having commenced that, she switched plan to secondary teacher education.<ref name="Sunday Times profile ANiS"/> She pursued further studies, securing a certificate in "English Language Teaching for Adults" in 2007.<ref name="UCD_profile_read23"/> and a Postgraduate Diploma in Education at [[Trinity College Dublin]].<ref name="Sunday Times profile ANiS">{{cite news |title=Profile: Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin  |work=Sunday Times |date=30 June 2013}}</ref><ref name="Indo_ivw_09">{{Cite news |last=Dwyer |first=Ciara |date=17 May 2009 |title=Aoibhinn Ni Shuilleabhain |work=The [[Irish Independent]] |url=https://www.independent.ie/woman/celeb-news/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-26536601.html |access-date=24 April 2023 |quote=... I teach an applied-maths class at 8am because it isn't on the school curriculum. ... Some day I would love to present a Tomorrow's World-style, science-based TV programme. ... In UCD, I got a Bord na Gaeilge scholarship for two years. It has one house on campus, where everybody speaks Irish. ...  I'm busy studying and Ryan is researching his book on JFK's visit to Ireland in the Sixties, so we both spend a lot of time in libraries}}</ref>

She worked from 2008 to 2011 as a student teacher, then a post-primary school teacher, of mathematics, physics and science, at St Mark's Community School in [[Tallaght]], a [[Education in the Republic of Ireland#Areas of disadvantage|DEIS]] school. She also taught Applied Mathematics, not on the school's curriculum, to interested students outside school hours.<ref name="UCD_profile_read23"/> She was an active supporter of the Department of Education's "Project Maths" concept of a new way of teaching and examining secondary school maths, and was a member of the department's working group on this for a period, being a "Modular Course Facilitator" from 2010 to 2014.<ref name="UCD_profile_read23"/>

She left teaching to pursue a Ph.D. in mathematics education, including improving approaches for science and maths teachers, in 2011, winning an Ussher Fellowship to fund multi-year doctoral studies.<ref name="KeenToMapANewWayForward">{{cite news |url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/education/2011/1129/1224308275944.html |title=Keen to map a new way forward |first=Aoibhinn |last=Ní Shúilleabháin |date=29 November 2011 |newspaper=[[The Irish Times]] |access-date=23 October 2019}}</ref><ref name="ThisMuchIKnow"/> She described her goals: "Over the next three years I'm hoping to design a new approach to continuous professional development for maths teachers. ... Based on the very successful Japanese model of CPD for teachers, I'm hoping to build a more collaborative approach, with teachers working together in groups to develop their classroom practice. It's common in many countries now but not here."<ref name="KeenToMapANewWayForward"/> She also critiqued current pressures on teachers of maths and scicence to "teach the exam", talking of her own school education and saying "inspirational teaching and learning is always a distraction from the exam preparation. It shouldn't be that way."<ref name="KeenToMapANewWayForward"/> From 2011 to 2013, she was "coordinator for Mathematics Pedagogy" in Trinity College's School of Education.<ref name="UCD_profile_read23"/> She completed the doctorate with the School of Education of [[Trinity College Dublin]] in 2014, with her thesis, "Developing mathematics teachers' pedagogical content knowledge through lesson study : a multiple case study at a time of curriculum change", published in 2015; she graduated that year.<ref name="ThisMuchIKnow">{{Cite news |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/lifestyle/features/this-much-i-know-aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-428996.html |title=This much I know: Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin |date=5 November 2016 |newspaper=[[Irish Examiner]] |access-date=2019-04-02}}</ref><ref name="Evoke_Oct21"/>

In August 2014 she became a faculty member of the School of Mathematics & Statistics at [[University College Dublin]] on a temporary assignment, and was hired as a regular lecturer after finalisation of her PhD,<ref name="Indo_150128">{{Cite news |title=A single rose: Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin looking forward to a brighter 2015 |url=https://www.independent.ie/style/celebrity/celebrity-features/a-single-rose-aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-looking-forward-to-a-brighter-2015-30944916.html |date=2015-01-28 |access-date=2023-04-21 |newspaper= The [[Irish Independent]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="IT_200905"/> researching and lecturing in mathematics and maths education.<ref name="siliconrepublic"/>  As  of 2021, she is an assistant professor at UCD,<ref name="Evoke_Oct21">{{Cite news |last=Quigley |first=Maeve |date=30 October 2021 |title=Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin says childcare is a 'huge' issue in Ireland as she returns to work |work=Evoke (online magazine) |url=https://evoke.ie/2021/10/30/news/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-says-childcare-is-a-huge-issue-in-ireland-as-she-returns-to-work |access-date=24 April 2023}}</ref> and is also director of the B.Sc. Science, Mathematics & Education initial teacher education programme in UCD's College of Science.<ref name="UCD_profile_read23">{{Cite web |title=Aoibhinn Ni Shuilleabhain (UCD People portal) |url=https://people.ucd.ie/aoibhinn.nishuilleabhain |access-date=2023-04-21 |website=University College Dublin (UCD)}}</ref> Nominated by colleagues from across the university, she won a 2020 UCD "Values in Action" award for her role as a socially engaged academic, communicator and leader.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 VIA Awards - Culture & Engagement |url=https://www.ucd.ie/engage/engagement/events/ucdawardspage/2020viaawards/ |access-date=2023-08-25 |website=www.ucd.ie}}</ref>

She has mentioned that she maintains her registration as a school teacher and might return to this career at some point.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Neill |first=Louise |date=2022 |title=Episode 12, Dr. Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin |url=https://www.teachersinspire.ie/en/stories/well-known-mathematician-and-broadcaster-dr-aoibhinn-n%C3%AD-sh%C3%BAilleabh%C3%A1in-discusses-her-passion-for-education-and-stem-in-particular |access-date=29 June 2023 |website=Teachers Inspire |publisher=[[Dublin City University]] (Faculty of Education) ([[Dermot Desmond]], [[Brian MacCraith]]) |publication-place=Drumcondra, Dublin}}</ref>

===Science communicator===
Known as a science communicator, especially in Ireland,<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/environment/the-oceans-are-rising-so-are-we-scientists-rally-in-dublin-1.3058073 |title='The oceans are rising, so are we': Scientists rally in Dublin |last=Power |first=Jack |date=22 April 2017 |newspaper=The Irish Times |language=en |access-date=2019-04-02}}</ref> and citing [[Richard Feynman]] as an influence,<ref name="SilRep_50WSci_10SciComms"/> Ní Shúilleabháin wrote a monthly column for the Science section of ''[[The Irish Times]]'' in 2016.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/science/how-to-draw-more-women-into-stem-1.2729542 |title=How to draw more women into STEM |date=28 July 2016 |last=Ní Shúilleabháin |first=Aoibhinn |newspaper=The Irish Times |language=en |access-date=2019-04-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/science/is-the-importance-of-female-role-models-in-science-overstated-1.3008212 |title=Is the importance of female role models in science overstated? |last=Ní Shúilleabháin |first=Aoibhinn |date=23 March 2017 |newspaper=The Irish Times |language=en |access-date=2019-04-02}}</ref>  She had previously co-curated an exhibition at [[Science Gallery Dublin]].<ref name="SciSquad_profile"/> She has delivered multiple science-related talks to schools.<ref name="UCD_profile_read23"/>

In 2016, [[Silicon Republic]] listed her as one of the 10 leading female science communicators, within it top "50 Women in Science",<ref name="SilRep_50WSci_10SciComms">{{Cite web |last=silicon |date=2016-11-17 |title=10 women who are strong science communicators |url=https://www.siliconrepublic.com/innovation/women-science-communicators |access-date=2023-04-25 |website=Silicon Republic |language=en}}</ref> and in 2017, she won an award for her ''Outstanding Communication of STEM'' from the national scientific research agency [[Science Foundation Ireland|SFI]].<ref name="siliconrepublic" /> She was co-chairperson of the ''Women in Mathematics in Ireland Day'' in 2018.<ref name="UCD_profile_read23"/>

In 2020 she received a [[Maths Week Ireland]] Award ''for outstanding work in raising public awareness of mathematics''.<ref name=2020_award>[https://www.irishtimes.com/news/science/aoibhinn-n%C3%AD-sh%C3%BAilleabh%C3%A1in-receives-2020-maths-week-ireland-award-1.4381047 Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin receives 2020 Maths Week Ireland award] The Irish Times, 14 October 2020</ref>

==Volunteer work and public service==
Ní Shúilleabháin has been a member of the advisory Leonardo Group at the [[Science Gallery]].  She has also been an "ambassador for science" in Ireland 2005–2006, and an "ambassador" for Dublin City of Science 2012.  She has also been both a host and a judge (from 2005 to 2010) at the BT [[Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition]].<ref name="SciSquad_profile">{{Cite web |title=Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin |url=http://www.thesciencesquad.ie/presenters/aoibhinn/ |access-date=2023-04-23 |website=The Science Squad |language=en}}</ref><ref name="UCD_profile_read23"/>

In 2017, she was invited to be a member of the executive committee of [[Women in Technology and Science|WITS]] (Women in Technology & Science) Ireland.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=European Young Leaders (#EYL40) |url=https://www.friendsofeurope.org/initiatives/european-young-leaders/ |access-date=2023-08-25 |website=Friends of Europe |language=en-US}}</ref>

She has been a director of Core Youth Services in Inchicore since 2021.<ref name="CoreYouth">{{Cite web |title=Meet the Board |url=https://www.core-ys.com/meet-the-board |access-date=2023-04-23 |website=Core Youth Services, Inchicore |language=en}}</ref>

In April 2022 Ní Shúilleabháin was nominated by the then [[Taoiseach]], Mícheál Martin to chair the national [[Citizens' Assembly (Ireland)|Citizens' Assembly]] on Biodiversity Loss.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Jim Gavin and Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin to chair new citizens' assemblies |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/jim-gavin-and-aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-to-chair-new-citizens-assemblies-1.4835155 |access-date=2023-08-25 |newspaper=The Irish Times |language=en}}</ref> The recommendations of the Assembly were published in March 2023 and its report was presented to Taoiseach [[Leo Varadkar]] in early April 2023; the report and recommendations will be reviewed by the Houses of the Oireachtas and the government, with a response due from government by the end of 2023.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Citizens' Assembly on biodiversity loss calls for switch to more plant-based diet |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/environment/climate-crisis/2023/04/05/citizens-assembly-on-biodiversity-loss-calls-for-switch-to-more-plant-based-diet/ |access-date=2023-08-25 |newspaper=The Irish Times |language=en}}</ref> She was nominated by the government as Ireland's representative at a special International Mother Earth Day meeting mandated by the General Assembly of the United Nations, the "12th Interactive Dialog of the United Nations General Assembly", and made a brief presentation of the work of the Citizens' Assembly and Ireland's position to the plenary session of this meeting before joining the interactive sessions.<ref name="UN_GA_presn_230424_1.37">{{cite AV media | people =Csaba Kőrösi ([[President of the United Nations General Assembly]]) - presiding, Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin - speaker, other official speakers | date = 24 April 2023 | title =12th Interactive Dialog of the United Nations General Assembly (Plenary Session) | type =Video | language =EN | url =https://media.un.org/en/asset/k1s/k1sei3i6c9 | access-date = | format =MP3 | time =1:37 | location =[[New York City|New York]] | publisher =[[United Nations]] | id = | oclc = | quote = }}</ref>

==Media career==
===Rose of Tralee 2005 contest===
Ní Shúilleabháin was crowned the 47th [[Rose of Tralee (festival)|Rose of Tralee]] on 23 August 2005, in a ceremony broadcast by [[RTÉ Television]].<ref name="WP050831">{{cite news |url=http://www.westernpeople.ie/news/story/?trs=cwgbidsnql |title=Carnacon's Aoibhinn wins the heart of a nation in Rose final |last=Esler |first=Cróna |date=31 August 2005 |newspaper=Western People |accessdate=22 February 2010 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120224070621/http://www.westernpeople.ie/news/story/?trs=cwgbidsnql |archivedate=24 February 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.independent.ie/national-news/a-rose-blooms-and-so-does-the-tv-show-246650.html |title=A Rose blooms: And so does the TV show |date=25 August 2005 |newspaper=Irish Independent |accessdate=22 February 2010 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023040319/http://www.independent.ie/national-news/a-rose-blooms-and-so-does-the-tv-show-246650.html |archivedate=23 October 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref> Ní Shúilleabháin was considered by bookmakers to be an early favourite to win the Rose of Tralee contest<ref name="II050824" /> and, as a result of a rules change, was the first Mayo Rose as final contestant in the history of the competition. She spent much of the following year on causes related to the win.<ref name="ThisMuchIKnow"/> She has stated that she owes much of her later media career to the opportunities opened up by her win.<ref name="Indo_140814_Owe">{{Cite news |last=Butler |first=Laura |date=14 August 2014 |title=Aoibhinn Ni Shuilleabhain: 'I owe the Rose of Tralee my career' |work=The [[Irish Independent]] |url=https://www.independent.ie/style/beauty/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-i-owe-the-rose-of-tralee-my-career-30508101.html |access-date=21 April 2023 |quote=...owes a lot to the event and the opportunities that came with being involved}}</ref>

===Broadcaster, 2005 to 2021===
Ní Shúilleabháin has worked as a broadcaster and host since her Rose of Tralee win. In 2007 she was a member of [[The Panel (Irish TV series)|''The Panel'']] on [[RTÉ Two]]<ref name="MN070814"/> and participated in the [[Celebrity Bainisteoir (season 1)|2008 season]] of ''[[Celebrity Bainisteoir]]'' on [[RTÉ One]], managing a [[Gaelic football]] team from [[Kiltimagh]] in her native Mayo.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.mayonews.ie/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=3588&Itemid=39 |title=A late, late show |last=Commins |first=Michael |date=4 March 2008 |newspaper=[[The Mayo News]] |accessdate=22 February 2010 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229142340/http://www.mayonews.ie/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=3588&Itemid=39 |archivedate=29 February 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2009 she hosted the weekly Irish music show ''The Reel Deal'' on RTÉ.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.independent.ie/national-news/tubridys-talented-other-half-is-the-reel-deal-1742080.html |title=Tubridy's talented other half is 'The Reel Deal' |last=Horan |first=Niamh |date=17 May 2009 |newspaper=Irish Independent |accessdate=22 February 2010 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090520152332/http://www.independent.ie/national-news/tubridys-talented-other-half-is-the-reel-deal-1742080.html |archivedate=20 May 2009 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/herald/aoibhinns-tv-ratings-show-shes-not-just-a-pretty-face/27917551.html |title=Aoibhinn's TV ratings show she's not just a pretty face |last=Finn |first=Melanie |date=8 July 2009 |newspaper=[[The Herald (Ireland)|Evening Herald]] |access-date=22 February 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090715134433/http://www.herald.ie/entertainment/around-town/aoibhinns-tv-ratings-show-shes-not-just-a-pretty-face-1811161.html |archive-date=15 July 2009 |url-status=live}}</ref> She also hosted regularly on Dublin's Irish language radio station, [[Raidió Na Life|Raidió na Life]],<ref name="Sunday Times profile ANiS"/> and stood in for [[Síle Seoige]] on [[Newstalk]] in 2011, interviewing [[Lee Child]] and [[Pixie Lott]], for example.<ref name="KeenToMapANewWayForward"/>

In 2012, she visited Uganda to report on [[Trócaire]]'s work there.<ref>{{Cite web |last=trocaire |date=2012-04-04 |title=Thanks for your support this Lent! |url=https://www.trocaire.org/news/thanks-for-your-support-this-lent/ |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=Trócaire |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ever wonder what good your Trocaire boxes do? Here's what... |url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/ever-wonder-what-good-your-trocaire-boxes-do-heres-what-36762965.html |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=independent |language=en}}</ref>

She has been a presenter of two flagship science programmes on RTÉ, ''The Science Squad'' from 2012 to 2014,<ref name="SciSquad">{{Cite web |date=2014 |title=The Science Squad |url=https://thesciencesquad.ie/ |access-date=22 April 2023 |website=The Science Squad}}</ref> and, from 2015 until 2021, ''10 Things to Know About...'',<ref name="10Things_site">{{Cite web |date=2023 |title=10 Things to Know About |url=https://10thingstoknowabout.ie/ |access-date=22 April 2023 |website=10 Things to Know About}}</ref> both with Jonathan McCrea and Kathriona Devereux.<ref name="ThisMuchIKnow"/><ref name="siliconrepublic">{{Cite web |url=https://www.siliconrepublic.com/innovation/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-science-communication-sfi |title=Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin furthers her quest to broaden the science conversation |last=O'Connell |first=Claire |date=2017-11-17 |website=Silicon Republic |language=en |access-date=2019-04-02}}</ref> She had previously stated, in 2009, "Some day I would love to present a [[Tomorrow's World]]-style, science-based TV programme."<ref name="Indo_ivw_09"/>

In 2013, she hosted her own [[RTÉ Radio 1]] lifestyle series ''Aoibhinn and Company'' as a summer replacement for [[Miriam O'Callaghan]]'s Sunday show ''Miriam Meets''.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.independent.ie/entertainment/tv-radio/in-miriams-shoes-aoibhinn-takes-over-rtes-sunday-slot-on-radio-one-29372703.html |title=In Miriam's shoes: Aoibhinn takes over RTE's Sunday slot on Radio 1 |first=Laura |last=Butler |date=26 June 2013 |newspaper=Irish Independent |access-date=23 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/herald/ability-not-tubs-got-me-summer-job-covering-for-miriam-says-aoibhinn/29374977.html |title=Ability, not Tubs, got me summer job covering for Miriam, says Aoibhinn |last=Sweeney |first=Ken |date=26 June 2013 |newspaper=[[The Herald (Ireland)|The Herald]] |access-date=23 October 2019}}</ref>

She presented the [[RTÉ]] travel show ''Getaways''<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rte.ie/tv/getaways |title=Getaways |website=RTÉ |access-date=23 October 2019 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140317073005/http://www.rte.ie/tv/getaways |archive-date=17 March 2014}}</ref> with Joe Lindsay for two series and presented the ''Fleadh Cheoil'' programme, with [[John Creedon]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rte.ie/tv/programmes/fleadh_cheoil.html |title=Fleadh Cheoil |website=RTÉ |access-date=23 October 2019 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140528113705/http://www.rte.ie/tv/programmes/fleadh_cheoil.html |archive-date=28 May 2014}}</ref> from 2014 to 2018.

==Music and writing==
Ní Shúilleabháin spent many years as a member of [[Comhaltas Ceoltóirí Éireann]], and won awards for [[sean-nós singing]], while also writing songs; she also won awards for poetry and short-story writing.<ref name="Green_n_Red_ivw"/>  In 2007 and 2008, she toured the United States, Japan, and Europe as the lead singer of Ragús, a traditional Irish music band.<ref name="MN070814">{{cite news |url=http://www.mayonews.ie/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=2169&Itemid=38 |title=Rose blooms |last=Duffy |first=Michael |date=14 August 2007 |newspaper=[[The Mayo News]] |accessdate=22 February 2010 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229142325/http://www.mayonews.ie/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=2169&Itemid=38 |archivedate=29 February 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="II090517">{{cite news |url=http://www.independent.ie/lifestyle/independent-woman/celebrity-news-gossip/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-1742123.html |title=Aoibhinn Ni Shuilleabhain |last=Dwyer |first=Ciara |date=17 May 2009 |newspaper=Irish Independent |accessdate=22 February 2010 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120129042313/http://www.independent.ie/lifestyle/independent-woman/celebrity-news-gossip/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-1742123.html |archivedate=29 January 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In addition to appointments, Ní Shúilleabháin was named as one of the "Top 100 Women in Science, Maths and Engineering" by Silicon Republic in 2014,<ref name="Top100_2014">{{Cite web |last=O’Dea |first=Ann |date=2014-03-11 |title=Women Invent: 100 top women in science, technology, engineering and maths - Part 1 - Careers {{!}} siliconrepublic.com - Ireland's Technology News Service |url=https://www.siliconrepublic.com/careers/women-invent-100-top-women-in-science-technology-engineering-and-maths-part-1 |access-date=2023-04-25 |website=Silicon Republic |language=en}}</ref> as one of the "40 under 40 European Young Leaders" by the Friends of Europe in 2017,<ref name="UCD_profile_read23"/> and on the "Top 100 Women of 2021" list by the [[Irish Examiner]] in 2021.<ref name="UCD_profile_read23"/>

==Publications==
Ní Shúilleabháin is one of four co-compilers of a 2012 science "short facts" book, ''A Neutron Walks Into a Bar'', published in aid of charity.<ref name="SciSquad_profile"/><ref name="ISBN_NeutronBar">{{Cite book |editor-last1=Delaney |editor-first1=Maria |editor-last2=Jones |editor-first2=Humphrey |editor-last3=Ní Shúilleabháin |editor-first3=Aoibhinn |editor-last4=O'Dwyer |editor-first4=Paul |title=A neutron walks into a bar - random facts and big ideas about our universe and everything in it (from the Science 140 thread)|date=2012 |publisher=Hachette Books Ireland |isbn=978-1-4447-4373-9 |location=Dublin, Ireland |oclc=809563187}}</ref> She is co-author of a paper for the 2014 annual conference of the Association for Teacher Education in Europe, "Investigating Representations of Ratio among Prospective Mathematics Teachers: a Study of Student-Teachers and Students of Mathematics in an Irish University".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Oldham |first1=E. |last2=Ni Shuilleabhain |first2=A. |date=2014 |editor-last=Arntzen |editor-first=E. |title=Investigating Representations of Ratio among Prospective Mathematics Teachers: a Study of Student-Teachers and Students of Mathematics in an Irish University |journal=ATEE 38th Annual Conference Papers |publisher=Association for Teacher Education in Europe |pages=298–321}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ní Shúilleabháin was in a relationship with broadcaster [[Ryan Tubridy]] from 2009 to 2014.<ref name="EH090506">{{cite web |url=http://goss.ie/showbiz/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-annoyed-ryan-tubridy-love-split-overshadows-her-college-graduation-21945 |title=Aoibhinn Ni Shuilleabhain annoyed Ryan Tubridy love-split overshadows her college graduation |last=Ryan |first=Ali |date=21 December 2014 |work=Goss |access-date=23 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/ireland/ryan-tubridy-and-aoibhinn-niacute-shuacuteilleabhaacutein-announce-split-303557.html |title=Ryan Tubridy and Aoibhinn Ni Shúilleabhain announce split |first=Dan |last=Buckley |date=20 December 2014 |newspaper=Irish Examiner |access-date=23 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.evoke.ie/showbiz/tubridy-breakup-ryan-and-aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-split/ |title=After FIVE years Ryan Tubridy and girlfriend Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin have broken up |date=20 December 2014 |work=Evoke.ie |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150203152043/http://www.evoke.ie/showbiz/tubridy-breakup-ryan-and-aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-split/ |archive-date=3 February 2015}}</ref> She married Carlos Diaz in a private ceremony in 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.independent.ie/style/celebrity/identity-of-aoibhinn-n-shilleabhins-mystery-groom-revealed-following-lowkey-wedding-36007395.html |title=Identity of Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin's mystery groom revealed following low-key wedding |date=7 August 2017 |newspaper=Irish Independent |access-date=2018-01-26 |language=en}}</ref> As of 2020, they have two sons.<ref name="Child_husbname">{{cite news |last1=Hyland |first1=Claire |title=Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin reveals first pics of six-week-old son Nisha (sic: actually Naoise) |url=https://evoke.ie/2019/03/09/showbiz/gossip/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-son-nisha-pics |accessdate=23 February 2020 |work=Evoke.ie |date=9 March 2019 |quote=revealed her son to the world yesterday. The presenter looked relaxed and content as she chatted and posed for photos with President Higgins at an event to mark International Women’s Day.}}</ref><ref name="evoke_201103">{{Cite news |last=Moran |first=Fionnuala |date=3 November 2020 |title=Dr Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin announces arrival of second child |work=Evoke (online magazine) |url=https://evoke.ie/2020/11/03/entertainment/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-second-child |access-date=21 April 2023}}</ref>

She has noted her continued interest in Irish culture and status as a Gaeilgeoir, stating "for me, Irish culture is so important. I dance, I play, I speak the language".<ref name="Indo_150128"/>  After living in Monkstown for more than 5 years, she moved to [[Inchicore]] in 2016.<ref name=Move>[https://goss.ie/showbiz/58147-2-58147 AOIBHINN NÍ SHÚILLEABHÁIN PURCHASES FIRST HOME SINCE RYAN TUBRIDY SPLIT] (Kendra Becker, 25 January 2016)</ref>

In September 2020, Ní Shúilleabháin spoke about her experience of being harassed and stalked, even beyond Dublin, over a two-year period, from 2015 to 2017, by Hans-Benjamin Braun, a fellow professor at [[University College Dublin|UCD]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=McGreevy |first=Ronan |date=8 September 2020 |title=UCD proposes new 'zero tolerance' policy to deal with sexual harassment |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/social-affairs/ucd-proposes-new-zero-tolerance-policy-to-deal-with-sexual-harassment-1.4349055 |access-date=2023-05-30 |newspaper=[[The Irish Times]] |language=en}}</ref> Despite many logged reports to the university's human resources function, and support from multiple colleagues, the problem continued and ultimately a report was made to the [[Garda Siochana]].  A prosecution for harassment eventually followed, in 2019, and the harasser was barred from making any contact with Ní Shúilleabháin for five years.<ref name="IT_200905">{{cite news|url= https://www.irishtimes.com/life-and-style/people/aoibhinn-n%C3%AD-sh%C3%BAilleabh%C3%A1in-two-years-of-harassment-at-ucd-1.4346015|title =Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin: Two years of harassment at UCD|date=5 September 2020 |newspaper=The Irish Times|accessdate=8 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.thejournal.ie/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-says-ucd-policies-on-harassment-need-to-be-victim-centred-5198740-Sep2020/|title =Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin says UCD policies on harassment need to be victim-centred|date=5 September 2020 |work=The Journal|accessdate=8 September 2020}}</ref> Her speaking out led to changes in UCD policy on sexual harassment and violence and to changes to national policies on this subject at Irish Higher Education Institutions. She eventually received a formal apology from the acting president of UCD in 2022; the perpetrator of the harassment had meantime left the university.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Aoibhinn Ní Shúilleabháin: 'It was important to me to get a formal apology from UCD' |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/life-style/people/2023/01/14/aoibhinn-ni-shuilleabhain-it-was-important-to-me-to-get-a-formal-apology-from-ucd/ |access-date=2023-08-25 |newspaper=The Irish Times |language=en}}</ref>
